name: HV 12816
description: A Cepheid in the Large Magellanic Cloud that pulsates every 9.11 days; its mean radius is 53.5 solar radii.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, HV 12816: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 53.5 +/- 3.6 (Monte-Carlo)

temperature.source: Groenewegen & Lub (2023), A&A 676, A136, VizieR J/A+A/676/A136/table1, Name=LMC4064, columns Teffp, e_Teffp: Teff 5875 +/- 88 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic)

distance.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, HV 12816: Baade-Wesselink distance (pc) 47026.6 +/- 3137.1 (Monte-Carlo)

color.reason: Interstellar dust reddens every spectrum of this star, E(B-V) = 0.07 +/- 0.005 (Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10), and its light changes through each pulsation

text.card: A Cepheid in the Large Magellanic Cloud that swells and shrinks every 9.1 days.
text.introduction: Its mean radius, 53.5 solar radii, comes from comparing how fast its surface moves with how its size changes, 47,027 parsecs away.

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius.
No dynamical mass is measured for this Cepheid; its mass is left unmeasured.
No surface gravity averaged over the pulsation is published, only single-phase values, so no limb darkening is drawn.
Its distance is the Baade-Wesselink one its radius was measured at, so the Magellanic Cepheids spread a few kiloparsecs in depth.

gravityRange.source: Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra)
